name: Long-duration Treasury hedge
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Protection When Growth Weakens
caseLead: Long-dated US Treasuries generally gain when growth expectations weaken or demand for safe assets rises, as falling yields increase their prices. The hedge benefits from Federal Reserve easing and demand for safe assets during growth slowdowns, but its effectiveness depends on whether inflation is also falling.
caseRest: Rising inflation can undermine the hedge because higher yields reduce bond prices, sometimes alongside falling equities. In 2022 long-dated Treasuries lost about 30 per cent while the S&P 500 fell about 18 per cent, so the hedge failed when it was needed. As a result, the strategy protects against falling growth but not against rising inflation or heavy government borrowing.
figNote: Each card shows the change in the US ten year Treasury yield over the episode, in basis points, where 100 basis points equal one percentage point. A fall in yield raises the price of long-dated bonds, so a negative figure benefits this strategy.

events.title: US downgrade drives investors into Treasuries
events.text: The US credit rating downgrade and euro area debt worries led investors to buy Treasuries, and the ten year yield fell about 60bp in August 2011. The strategy gained because lower yields raised the price of long-dated bonds.

events.title: Brexit vote pushes Treasury yields to record lows
events.text: The June 2016 vote to leave the European Union led investors to buy Treasuries, and the ten year yield fell about 40bp to a record low in early July. The strategy gained because long-dated bonds rose in price by more than shorter-dated ones.

events.title: Covid crash lifts Treasuries then forces selling
events.text: The ten year Treasury yield fell about 100bp to 0.5 per cent by 9 March 2020 as investors expected emergency rate cuts. Results were mixed because the yield rose back above 1 per cent within nine days when funds sold Treasuries to raise cash.

events.title: Inflation and Fed rate rises hit long bonds
events.text: Higher inflation, energy prices after Russia's invasion of Ukraine and Fed rate rises lifted the ten year yield about 270bp between the end of 2021 and October 2022. The strategy lost heavily because stocks and bonds fell together, so Treasuries gave no protection.

events.title: Bank failures push investors into Treasuries
events.text: The failures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank in March 2023 led the ten year yield to fall about 60bp in under two weeks. The strategy gained because long-dated bonds rose in price as markets priced in Fed rate cuts.

events.title: US tariffs push Treasury yields higher
events.text: After the April 2025 tariff announcement, the ten year yield rose about 50bp in a week even as equities fell. The strategy lost because long-dated Treasuries did not hedge equity losses, as investors sold US assets.

instrument: US Treasury bonds, ETFs and futures with 20 years or more to maturity; rolled quarterly
rules: Constant duration of about 17 years; position halved if the ten year yield rises 100bp in three months; inflation-linked bonds held as a partial offset
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads, fund fees and futures roll costs deducted
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from bond price gains to inflation risk control

legs.purpose: Provides margin and earns the cash rate

entry: Bonds bought when inflation expectations are below 3%
size: Set to an 11% annualised volatility target
exit: Rebalanced quarterly to the target duration
stop: Position halved if the ten year yield rises 100bp in three months
marketWatch: Inflation expectations, the Fed's expected policy rate path and the supply of new Treasury bonds are the main indicators, because they determine whether yields fall when growth weakens. Scheduled inflation releases, central bank meetings and fiscal announcements can change the yield curve quickly. Rehyn also watches the correlation between stocks and bonds, because a positive correlation reduces the hedge.

favourable.heading: Banking or growth scares
favourable.text: Sudden growth fears favour the strategy because investors expect the Fed to cut rates and buy Treasuries, which pushes down yields on long-dated bonds. In March 2023 the ten year yield fell about 60bp in under two weeks as bank failures raised expectations of rate cuts.

favourable.heading: Geopolitical stress with low inflation
favourable.text: Geopolitical stress favours the strategy when inflation is low because investors buy US government bonds as a safe asset. After the vote to leave the European Union in June 2016, the ten year yield fell to a record low.

favourable.heading: Falling inflation expectations
favourable.text: Lower inflation expectations favour the strategy because they allow the Fed to cut rates and raise the value of fixed coupons. In 2019 the ten year yield fell from about 2.7 per cent to about 1.9 per cent and long-dated Treasuries returned more than 10 per cent.

adverse.heading: Inflation and aggressive rate rises
adverse.text: Rising inflation hurts the strategy because investors demand higher yields and long-dated bonds lose the most value. In 2022 long-dated Treasuries lost about 30 per cent as the ten year yield rose about 270bp.

adverse.heading: Stocks and bonds falling together
adverse.text: A positive correlation between stocks and bonds hurts the strategy because bonds fall at the same time as equities and no longer hedge them. In April 2025 the ten year yield rose about 50bp in a week while equities fell sharply.

adverse.heading: Heavy government borrowing
adverse.text: Heavy government borrowing hurts the strategy because investors demand higher yields to hold more long-dated debt. Between August and October 2023, rising Treasury issuance and Fed rate guidance lifted the ten year yield to 5 per cent, its highest level since 2007.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's return over each event window, measured from the last market high before the shock to the market low using the default backtest parameters above. Positive figures mean Treasuries gained while equities fell.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in the S&P 500, inflation expectations and Treasury yields, which are then applied to the strategy's current bond and futures positions.
